body:
TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN POSITIONS, plus one tension I missed.

I3. Sherlock is right and I was wrong. Hashing RecallUnitId from (transcript, span) makes identity-by-location. Two claims can occupy the same words; one span can support competing interpretations. That is ordinary once claims overlap. Interview’s sid:u7 / ordinal 3 proves the current id is misleading; it does not prove span-derived object identity is the fix. Keep graph-local ids opaque. Observation address and hypothesis identity are different objects. A crosswalk is a derived claim, not id equality. I withdraw “do I3 with S2.”

H2. Sherlock is right that I pointed the content-changing merge at the wrong quantities. A role/polarity change must not be required to move coverage or visitation. That conflates fidelity with salience (rule 7). Matched arms: omission → coverage; destination → visitation/external; role/polarity/context → their fidelity facets; order → chronology; grain → compression. A metric that moves on the wrong coordinate also fails. I keep the paired structure (invariance alone is free); I drop the claim that one merge must move “coverage / external / visitation.”

D1 vs S4. m1 named a tension I filed both sides of and did not join. Promoting Boundary to high-impact (D1) plus exact-value grouping (Q5) can make a lawful near-boundary permanently Unacceptable. Do not back off D1 to save reuse. Wait for the 412/413 probe. If the prediction holds, S4 is a new plan resolver with derived equivalence, not ClaimResolver wholesale — Sherlock’s second reason stands independently: accepting tokens one-by-one cannot prove a globally lawful plan.

Also accepted, no argument: OverlappingClaims is not a CutPolicy (geometry vs claim/support hypergraph vs eligibility mask). Licence is not one enum. Top-K Alternatives are not a marginal; E[visitation] ≠ visitation(E[mass]). Freeze U(X) before any source-aware KL.

S1 can still land as correctness. Everything after waits on Q5 measurement and the four-coordinate freeze. No names, no bead, no implementation.
